title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page titled 'Unités'. Let K be a number field embedded in C. Claim: the following are equivalent. (a) Every unit ε of K has some positive power ε^n that is real. (b) Either K ⊂ R, or K = K0(α) with K0 totally real, α² ∈ K0 and α² totally negative. In modern terms, (b) says K is real or K is a CM field.

Proof of (a) ⇒ (b). Suppose K ⊄ R and set K' = K ∩ R, so [K:K'] = p ≥ 2. Let (r1, r2) and (r1', r2') be the signatures of K and K'. Then:
- Degrees give r1 + 2r2 = p(r1' + 2r2').
- Condition (a) says E_K/E_{K'} is torsion, so by Dirichlet the unit ranks agree: r1 + r2 = r1' + r2'.
- Eliminating r2: 0 = r1 + (p−2)r1' + (2p−2)r2' ≥ r1 + 2r2'.
- Hence r1 = r2' = 0, so K' is totally real and K is totally imaginary. Implicitly (p−2)r1' = 0, so p = 2.
- Writing K = K'(α), each real embedding of K' extends only to complex embeddings of K, so α² is totally negative.

Proof of (b) ⇒ (a). Here K' = K0, r1 = r2' = 0 and r2 = r1', so the unit ranks agree. Then E_K/E_{K'} is finite, giving (a).

Example: K = Q(ζ_m). Since K/Q is abelian, complex conjugation lies in the Galois group, so its fixed field K ∩ R is Galois and hence totally real, while K is totally imaginary (for m > 2). So cyclotomic fields satisfy (a).

The page belongs to the 'Galois theory of motives' file. There, CM fields, and the fact that units (and Weil numbers) of CM fields are real up to roots of unity, govern the structure of motives with CM / the Serre group. This is presumably the purpose of this lemma.
errors: The definition of r2 (resp. r2') reads 'la moitié du nombre de conjugués imaginaires de K'' for both; it should be of K (resp. K').
'[K:K']=2' is a leftover from before the author replaced 'quadratique' with 'de degré p≥2'. The degree is p, as the next formula correctly uses.

Gap: the proof never says explicitly that p = 2. This follows from 0 = r1 + (p−2)r1' + (2p−2)r2' together with r1' ≥ 1 (K' is totally real and nonzero-dimensional), and it is needed to write K = K0(α) with α² ∈ K0.
For the example, the case m ≤ 2 (K = Q, real) is trivially covered by the first alternative in (b); otherwise the argument is correct.

ideas.what: A non-real number field has a proper subfield of the same unit rank (equivalently, every unit is real up to a power) iff it is a CM field (totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real field).
ideas.modern_name: Unit-rank characterization of CM fields (Remak's theorem on fields with unit defect)
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Remak (1950s); standard in texts on cyclotomic fields (e.g. Washington, Ch. 4)

ideas.what: Cyclotomic fields are CM since the maximal real subfield of an abelian field is totally real.
ideas.modern_name: Q(ζ_m) is CM; Q(ζ_m)^+ totally real

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct (up to small slips) textbook proof of the classical unit-rank characterization of CM fields. It is presumably preparatory to work on CM motives / the Serre group, but contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out word before 'ou bien K⊂R' is illegible (struck), not part of the statement.
In the definition of r2: the manuscript indeed says 'de K'' — an author slip; it should read 'de K'.
'[K:K']=2' is as written in the manuscript (author slip; should be p).
